subject: Re: OrbitX RFP - Reservation throughput & compute profile deep-dive
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@orbitx.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitx.com
Date: 2026-11-21T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: OrbitX RFP - throughput targets and reservation planning

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infrastructure and ML teams reviewed Redwood's overview and have a few follow-ups to include in the RFP: a detailed compute profile for dedicated reservations (GPU families supported, expected tokens/sec targets per model tier, recommended baseline vs burst slotting), and — importantly — a proposal for a 12-month phasing plan that lets us start with a smaller commitment and scale deterministically.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our infra team asking for per-model throughput assumptions and warmup expectations. Can you confirm you can provide a completed response by end of the week? Also: include any guardrails you recommend for tail-latency and cold-KV-cache behavior.

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitX
[Attachment: orbitx_rfi_questionnaire_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@orbitx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OrbitX RFP - throughput targets and reservation planning

Alice — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. We can absolutely deliver the per-model compute profile and a 12-month ramp plan.

High level notes up front (we'll include the full matrix in the attached spreadsheet):
- GPU families recommended: A100 40GB (dense baseline), H100 80GB (latency-critical and heavy-context models), and a quantized L40s-style tier for cost-sensitive batch workloads. We'll show slot equivalencies and packing efficiency per family.
- Tokens/sec: baseline expectations assume 8k context average for your large-context use cases; we'll publish median and P95 tokens/sec for sample workloads.
- Burst corridor: propose a 2x burst for the first 3 months, then a traffic-based auto-burst policy tied to utilization thresholds.
- Warmup/KV-cache: plan for an initial KV-warmup window (30–120s depending on traffic skew) and suggest pre-warming options for scheduled spikes.

I'll attach our draft compute-profile matrix and a simulated throughput model. If you want a short sync, I'm available Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserve_compute_profile_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 128KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: OrbitX RFP - throughput targets and reservation planning

Folks — forwarding OrbitX's RFI. Key asks: per-model tokens/sec (median & P95), recommended GPU family mapping, and a 12-month reservation phasing that supports a low-entry commit then predictable scaling.

Questions I want input on before we finalize the spreadsheet:
1) For their baseline models (we saw a mix of Llama2-13B and a 70B customer-tuned model in the demo), should we recommend starting them on A100s or go straight to H100 for tail-latency headroom? My draft suggests A100 baseline with selective H100 lanes for 70B at P95 < 250ms.
2) Do we want to propose a price-tiered burst lane (reserved burst tokens at ~1.4x list) or an autoscaling overage model?
3) What pre-warm guidance should we include for SST-style conversational workloads that exhibit heavy long-tail context reuse?

I've attached the initial matrix; please annotate and send back by EOD so I can consolidate.

Soojin
[Attachment: reserve_compute_profile_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 128KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrbitX RFP - throughput targets and reservation planning

Thanks for the send, Soojin. I made inline comments in the matrix and a small supplemental CSV that models tokens/sec vs slot size for the three GPU families. High-level recommendations:
- Start OrbitX on a mixed baseline: 60% A100 40GB, 30% L40s-quant (or equivalent) for batch embedding/low-cost traffic, 10% H100 80GB as a latency reserve. That gives a predictable base while keeping a path to scale low-cost inference.
- For the 70B tuned model: if they require P95 < 250ms at 8k context, H100 is the only practical baseline. Recommend 1:10 allocation (one H100 slot per 10 A100 slots) and a canary policy for production rollout.
- Burst policy: propose an explicit reserved-burst pool (20% of baseline) priced at 1.35x and an autoscaling overage with a soft cap (2.5x) for emergency spikes. This balances cost predictability with operational flexibility.
- KV-cache warmup: recommend a hybrid approach — automatic prefix caching for frequent prompts (configured by top-N prompt sets) and a scheduled pre-warm contract for predicted events. Include guidance on TTL and eviction to keep memory efficient.

I've attached throughput_model_epoch3.csv with simulated tail-latency curves and slot-efficiency numbers. Please review the numbers in column D-F (tokens/sec median/P95/P99) before we send to OrbitX.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throughput_model_epoch3.csv (csv, 36KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@orbitx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, procurement@orbitx.com
Date: 2026-11-23T14:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OrbitX RFP - reservation throughput & compute profile deep-dive

Alice — thanks for the patience. Attached is our completed response to the questionnaire along with the compute-profile spreadsheet and a simple throughput model. Summary of deliverables (high level):

1) Compute profile matrix (reserve_compute_profile_v2.xlsx) — maps your model tiers to recommended GPU families, slot equivalence, expected tokens/sec median/P95 for baseline and burst lanes, and packing efficiency assumptions.
2) Throughput model (throughput_model_epoch3.csv) — simulated tails and slot-scaling curves we used to size the phasing plan.
3) Phasing proposal (embedded in the spreadsheet) — a 12-month plan that starts with a 25% baseline commit (mix: 60% A100 / 30% L40s-quant / 10% H100), scales to 60% commit at month 6, and reaches full target by month 12. The plan includes: monthly check-ins, canary policy for H100 allocations, and a reserved-burst pool sized at 20% of baseline priced at 1.35x.

Operational guardrails and notes:
- Tail-latency: we provide per-model P95/P99 targets in the sheet. For the 70B tuned model we recommend an H100 lane to meet P95 < 250ms at 8k context; fallback to quantized L40s at higher latency is possible for non-critical batches.
- KV-cache: initial warmup window 30–90s for conversational traffic with a top-N prefix pre-warm contract for known spikes. We include recommended TTLs and eviction heuristics in the matrix.
- Auto-burst vs reserved-burst: recommended hybrid (reserved-burst pool + soft autoscale) to limit billing surprises while keeping headroom for traffic variability.

Next steps I propose: 30–45 minute technical sync to walk the matrix and confirm assumptions, then procurement-friendly version of the spreadsheet for signature (we can convert to CSV/DocuSign-ready format). I'm available Tuesday/Wednesday next week 9–11am PT.

If you'd like, we can also run a short pilot week where we instrument telemetry and validate the slot-efficiency numbers against your actual prompt mix — that usually reduces mismatch risk during the first months of a committed reserve.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
